# frozen_string_literal: true

# An immutable amount stored in integer cents. Assumes two decimal places.
class Money
  include Comparable

  attr_reader :cents, :currency

  def initialize(cents, currency = "USD")
    raise ArgumentError, "cents must be an Integer" unless cents.is_a?(Integer)
    unless currency.is_a?(String) && currency.match?(/\A[A-Z]{3}\z/)
      raise ArgumentError, "currency must be a three-letter uppercase code"
    end

    @cents = cents
    @currency = currency.dup.freeze
    freeze
  end

  def <=>(other)
    return nil unless other.instance_of?(self.class) && currency == other.currency

    cents <=> other.cents
  end

  def ==(other)
    (self <=> other) == 0
  end
  alias eql? ==

  def hash
    [self.class, cents, currency].hash
  end

  def to_s
    whole, fraction = cents.abs.divmod(100)
    sign = cents.negative? ? "-" : ""
    amount = "#{whole}.#{fraction.to_s.rjust(2, '0')}"
    currency == "USD" ? "#{sign}$#{amount}" : "#{currency} #{sign}#{amount}"
  end
end

Implemented an immutable `Money` value object in `money.rb`. It stores amounts as integer cents, defaults to USD, and supports value equality, hash keys, and ordering within the same currency. Different currencies are not comparable.

```ruby
Money.new(105) == Money.new(105)  # => true
Money.new(105) < Money.new(200)   # => true
Money.new(-105).to_s              # => "-$1.05"
Money.new(105, "EUR").to_s        # => "EUR 1.05"
```
